Condo & HOA management in Evanston.

Evanston is the North Shore's most vibrant lakefront city, home to Northwestern University, a thriving downtown, and an exceptional mix of vintage lakefront condominiums, mid-century courtyard buildings, and modern transit-oriented developments. Property management in Evanston requires fluency with the city's own landlord-tenant and building regulations layered on top of Illinois condominium law. We serve Evanston associations with the responsive, detail-driven management its engaged, well-informed boards expect.

What managing Evanston takes.

A second rulebook

Evanston layers its own property-maintenance standards and rental-registration rules on top of Illinois condominium law. We keep boards, and owners who lease their units, on the right side of both City Hall and the statute.

Lakefront vintage to downtown towers

From vintage courtyard condominiums near the lakefront to transit-oriented towers by the Davis Street Metra and CTA stops, Evanston's stock spans a century of construction. Our capital planning spans it too.

Engaged, well-informed boards

Evanston boards read the financials. We deliver monthly reporting detailed enough for the university-town scrutiny this community is known for, and answer the follow-up questions gladly.

Evanston boards ask us first.

Does Evanston regulate condo associations differently than Chicago?

Evanston enforces its own property-standards and rental-registration ordinances alongside the Illinois Condominium Property Act, so compliance looks different than it does across the border in Chicago. We manage Evanston associations with those local requirements built into day-to-day operations.

Does CenterPoint manage associations in Evanston?

Yes. CenterPoint Association Management provides condominium, HOA, and townhome association management in Evanston (ZIP 60201, 60202). Every association gets a dedicated manager, monthly financial reporting, and board support grounded in Illinois association law.

How much does association management cost in Evanston?

Management starts at $20 per unit per month, quoted as a flat monthly fee based on your association's size, building systems, financial complexity, and service scope. It is never a percentage of your budget. See pricing for what drives the fee.

How does a Evanston association switch to CenterPoint?

Plan on a managed 30 to 60 day transition after your board gives notice under its current contract. We retrieve records from the outgoing manager, set up banking and vendor relationships, notify owners, and open board and resident access. Call 773.728.0652 or .

How should a Evanston board compare management companies?

Compare at least three firms on the same terms: an active Illinois community association management firm license, a licensed manager, a flat monthly fee in writing, after-hours emergency coverage, and a written transition plan. Our free proposal scorecard helps boards score proposals side by side.
